vsterraindiffusion:command-elevation: Show the model elevation and climate at your position
vsterraindiffusion:configsep-inference-t: How the model runs is set per world, in the Terrain Diffusion tab of the Customize screen. These tune caches and logging on this machine.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-TerrainSample: How this mod answers Algernon's Terrain Sampler, which other mods use to predict terrain without generating it. "full" builds the model's terrain around the position: exact, but runs the model for ground not generated yet, and the asking mod waits for it. "coarse" answers from the coarse model alone: blurred to about 512 blocks, but far cheaper. Takes effect immediately.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-TerrainTileSi: Side length in blocks of the terrain generated per model query. Zero chooses 128 on CPU and 256 on GPU. Larger spreads the model's latency over more chunks, at the cost of a longer stall on first visit. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-TerrainTileCa: Megabytes of finished terrain tiles to keep. This has to cover everything world generation touches at once - a spawn area alone can span a hundred tiles - or tiles are evicted while still in use and get rebuilt from scratch. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-TileCacheMega: Total megabytes of decoded tensor windows kept across all pipeline stages. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-LatentBatchSi: Latent windows sent through the base model together. Zero chooses one on CPU and four on GPU. Larger batches can improve GPU utilisation but need more working memory. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-DebugMapPort-: Port for the debug map, a read-only web page showing the model's heightmap and climate maps as tiles are generated. 0, the default, opens no port at all. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-DebugMapBindA: Address the debug map listens on. Loopback by default, so only this machine can reach it; 0.0.0.0 exposes the world's terrain and climate to anything that can reach the port. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-DebugMapHisto: How many generated tiles the debug map remembers, at about eight kilobytes each. The oldest are dropped past this. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-VerboseInfere: Log a line at notification level for every terrain tile generated. Very noisy; useful when profiling. With this off those lines still go to the debug log, and the main log gets one only when a tile stalls - a second or more, and four times the session average. Applies immediately.
vsterraindiffusion:configsep-heightandsc: How the model's metres become blocks. Changes the shape of the world: new chunks will not match ones already generated. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenHeigh: "isotropic" makes a block as tall as it is wide, so the landscape is at true scale in every direction. "manual" uses the metres per block below. "auto" measures the region's peaks once per world and stretches the terrain to fill the world height, which suits short worlds at the cost of exaggerated relief.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenMeter: Manual height mode only: metres of elevation per block. Zero falls back to isotropic.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenScale: Overrides the world's "Resolution" setting. Zero uses the world setting; values above 6 are only reachable from here.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenVerti: Overrides the world's "Vertical exaggeration" setting. Zero uses the world setting. In auto height mode this multiplies the calibrated height rather than setting it outright.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenLinea: Fraction of the available height mapped perfectly linearly. Above the knee the curve bends over so arbitrarily tall model peaks still fit under the ceiling; closer to 1 means more faithful summits and harder clipping.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenOcean: Fraction of the space below sea level that the deepest ocean reaches.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenShore: Extra block rows per unit of the model's own height (the square root of metres) at the waterline, on land and sea floor. The model's heights crush the first few metres of every coast into one wide flat row; this gives coasts an even slope and shelving shallows instead. 0 turns it off. Applies to worlds created after the change; existing worlds keep what they were generated with.
How far the shore detail reaches, in square-root-of-metres: it falls by a factor of e every this many units, so at 3 it is mostly gone by 60 m. Applies to worlds created after the change.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenSlope: Multiplies the Perlin detail added to sloped ground. The model resolves features down to one native pixel, so hillsides need roughness of their own; raise for craggier slopes.
vsterraindiffusion:configsep-heightcalib: Only used when the height mode is "auto". Changes the shape of the world: new chunks will not match ones already generated. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenTarge: How much of the space between sea level and the world ceiling the region's tall peaks should occupy. Leave a little room, or the summits flatten against the ceiling.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenPeakQ: Which elevation quantile counts as a "tall peak". 0.995 means the top half percent of the surveyed area reaches the ceiling; lowering it makes the whole landscape taller and clips more summits.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenCalib: Half-width in blocks of the area surveyed around spawn. This should cover the part of the world you expect to explore: surveying a whole continent lets a distant mountain range decide the scale and leaves your own surroundings flat.

How many full-detail probes to run on the tallest surveyed cells. The survey only sees terrain averaged over several kilometres, so peaks need measuring at full resolution. Each probe costs about as much as one terrain tile, once per world.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenRelie: Assumed ratio of true peak height to the coarse survey's value, used when probing is disabled or fails.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenMinAu: Lower bound on the vertical exaggeration calibration is allowed to choose.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenMaxAu: Upper bound on the vertical exaggeration calibration is allowed to choose.
vsterraindiffusion:configsep-climate-tex: How the model's bioclimatic variables become the world's temperature and rainfall. Changes the shape of the world: new chunks will not match ones already generated. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenClima: Overrides how much of the climate the model drives: "full" for model temperature, rainfall and vegetation, "off" to leave Vintage Story's climate alone. Empty uses the world's own setting.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenRainf: What the game's 0-255 rainfall byte is built from. "moisture" uses the model's aridity - precipitation measured against how much the climate can evaporate - which is what actually decides whether ground is bare. "precipitation" uses annual millimetres alone.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenMoist: Moisture basis: the tree-moisture value that maps to the middle of the rainfall scale.
Moisture basis: spread of log tree-moisture across the model's land.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenRainf: Precipitation basis: annual millimetres that map to the middle of the rainfall scale.
Precipitation basis: spread of the model's log precipitation over land.

Shifts every place's rainfall by the same amount, leaving the model's own answer alone at zero. Raise for a wetter world, lower for a drier one. This is the setting to reach for first: unlike the moisture calibration it moves wet and dry ground equally, instead of turning already-dry regions into desert.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenTempe: Degrees Celsius added to every model temperature, for a warmer or colder world.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenGloba: How much of the world's "Global temperature" and "Global precipitation" settings is built into the climate the model is conditioned on. The rest is applied afterwards, so the world reads the same either way; what changes is whether the model knew. At 1 an arid world is drawn as an arid world, with the drainage, vegetation and soils to match.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenClima: How much noise the model is told the shifted climate carries. Lower binds it more tightly, the opposite of what the name suggests. Only consulted when the global climate settings are off their defaults. Zero uses the model's own value.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenLatit: How much of a north-south climate gradient the world gets. The model's climate has continents, maritime coasts and rain shadows in it but nothing that knows which way is north; at 1 the equator, subtropical deserts, storm track and ice caps are conditioned in at the latitudes the game says they belong, and everything the model knows about coasts and mountains happens within those bands.
vsterraindiffusion:configsep-seasons-tex: How the year swings. Changes the shape of the world: new chunks will not match ones already generated. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenSeaso: Swing temperature through the year using the model's temperature seasonality rather than latitude alone. Continental interiors then get hard winters and hot summers while maritime and tropical climates at the same latitude stay even.
Multiplies the modelled seasonal temperature swing. Zero gives a world with no seasons.
Swing rainfall through the year using the model's precipitation seasonality, so monsoon climates get a real wet and dry season rather than drizzling evenly all year.
Multiplies the modelled wet and dry season contrast.

Least share of a place's yearly rainfall the dry season falls to. Only bites in the most strongly seasonal climates. Lower keeps their dry seasons sharpest; they then go months with no rain, and unirrigated crops there stop growing until the rains return.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenTrans: How long a translocator may wait for terrain that never arrived before starting its search again. The server gives up on generating a search candidate if it cannot pause worldgen in time, which otherwise leaves the translocator stuck on "Warping spacetime..." until its chunk is reloaded. 0 turns the watchdog off.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenRiver: How far the land is lowered where the Rivers mod runs a river, so the model shapes a valley to carry it instead of a ridge to cut through. Needs that mod. 0 leaves the landscape alone; high values sink river corridors below sea level and turn them into inlets.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenTrans: How long the server may wait for terrain generation to come to a stop before inspecting a candidate location. The game allows 3.6 seconds, which modelled terrain regularly exceeds; when it runs out the work already done is thrown away and the search starts over. 0 keeps the game's own limit.

Caps how far a translocator looks for its partner. A shorter range links faster, because it searches ground that is more likely already generated, but the hops it makes are shorter. 0 keeps the game's own 8000 blocks. Links already made are kept.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenSeaso: Swing the year the opposite way south of the equator. Vintage Story's calendar already does this, so turning it off does not give the world one hemisphere - it gives it a southern hemisphere whose leaves fall in the spring.
vsterraindiffusion:configsep-vegetationa: What grows on the terrain and what it is made of. Changes the shape of the world: new chunks will not match ones already generated. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenFores: Scales the forest cover the model's moisture implies. Trees on the ground go as the square of this, because vanilla accepts each candidate tree with probability (byte/255)^2, so 1.4 is about twice the trees. The byte also saturates, which is why much above 1.2 only flattens the wet end.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenShrub: Scales shrub cover the same way, with the same squaring.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenFores: How far vanilla's patchy forest noise opens the model's woods into fields and glens. About a third of vanilla's map is open ground, in patches roughly a kilometre across; this thins the trees there by this fraction. 0 turns it off, 1 leaves those patches bare. Applies to newly generated land.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenBaseR: How much of the base model's first draw its second step throws away and redraws. 0.35 is what the model's author found best for image quality; higher redraws more of the medium-scale relief, lower keeps the first draw. Changes newly generated terrain.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenResca: Stretch the altitude bands of vanilla's surface block layers to match the terrain height, so hills that are only tall because of vertical exaggeration are not surfaced as bare alpine gravel. No effect at isotropic scale.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenBareS: Leave slopes too steep to hold soil as bare rock. The threshold comes from the model's own moisture, because roots are what keep a hillside from shedding its soil.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenGlaci: Cap ground whose warmest month never rises above freezing with glacier ice, so ice fields look permanent rather than like a winter that has not melted yet.
vsterraindiffusion:configsep-coastlines-: How the world's ocean map and the model's terrain are made to agree. Changes the shape of the world: new chunks will not match ones already generated. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenOcean: "input" conditions the model on the ocean map, so the world's land cover and ocean scale settings - and any ocean map another mod installs - decide where the sea is. "output" is the reverse: the model invents its own continents and the ocean map is rewritten to match, which ignores the world settings and overwrites other mods' maps.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenLandm: Input mode: how completely the ocean map overrides the model's own sense of where land belongs. Below 1 the map biases the coastline rather than setting it, which keeps more of the model's structure at the cost of honouring the world settings less exactly.

Input mode: how much noise the model is told the landmask carries. Lower binds it more tightly, the opposite of what the name suggests. The model ships 0.5, at which it reproduces the ocean map over about 88% of the world; 0.1 gets that to 95%. Zero uses the model's own value.
vsterraindiffusion:configsep-spawn-text: Where the world drops you. Takes effect on the next server start.
vsterraindiffusion:setting-WorldGenStart: Honour the world's "Starting climate" setting by placing spawn on land whose modelled temperature falls in the chosen band. Vanilla implements that setting by shifting its own climate map, which cannot be done to a model that predicts a specific world, so the player moves instead.
How far from the middle of the map the search may look, in blocks. It stops as soon as it finds matching land, so this is only where it gives up and takes the closest temperature it saw.

How much more reluctant the search is to move spawn north or south than east or west. Distance along Z decides day length and, past the world's polar distance, buys midnight sun and polar night; distance along X costs nothing.
